text_blocks.snippet: Jardiance (empagliflozin) can cause both common and serious side effects. Because the medication works by helping your kidneys flush out extra sugar through your urine, many side effects involve urination, fluid balance, and genital or urinary tract areas.
snippet_highlighted_words: urination, fluid balance, and genital or urinary tract areas

text_blocks.snippet: You can find more detailed safety information on the Boehringer Ingelheim Jardiance Resource Page.

list.snippet: Urinary tract infections (UTIs): Symptoms include burning, urgency, frequency, or cloudy/bloody urine.

Genital yeast infections: Vaginal yeast infections in women (itching, thick white discharge, swelling) and yeast infections around the penis in men (redness, itching, pain, or strong-smelling discharge).
Increased urination: Going to the bathroom to pee more often or in larger amounts.

text_blocks.snippet: Serious Side Effects (Require Prompt Medical Attention)

list.snippet: Dehydration: Loss of too much body water and salt, leading to dizziness, lightheadedness, weakness, or fainting—especially when standing up. Risk is higher if you take water pills (diuretics), are 65 or older, have kidney issues, or follow a low-salt diet.

Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA): A dangerous buildup of acid and ketones in the blood, which can happen even if blood sugar is under 250 mg/dL. Symptoms include nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, unusual tiredness, fruity-smelling breath, and trouble breathing.

Low blood sugar (Hypoglycemia): More likely if you take Jardiance alongside other diabetes medications like insulin or sulfonylureas. Symptoms include shakiness, fast heartbeat, confusion, sweating, and weakness.

Necrotizing fasciitis (Fournier’s gangrene): A rare, life-threatening bacterial infection of the tissue under the skin between the anus and genitals, causing severe pain, swelling, redness, and fever.
Lower limb amputations: Increased risk of toe, foot, or leg amputation, particularly if you have a history of amputations, peripheral vascular disease, or diabetic foot ulcers.
Serious allergic reactions: Rash, hives, or swelling of the face, lips, tongue, and throat.
